title: Personalized Federated Continual Learning via Multi-Granularity Prompt

problem.claim: Personalized Federated Continual Learning requires both global spatial-temporal knowledge fusion and client-specific model improvement.

gap.claim: Existing personalized federated learning and federated continual learning methods overlook multi-granularity knowledge representation for addressing spatial-temporal catastrophic forgetting and personalization.

contributions.claim: Introduces a multi-granularity prompt consisting of a coarse-grained global prompt and a fine-grained local prompt.
Designs a selective prompt fusion mechanism to aggregate knowledge from global prompts distilled from different clients.
Uses exclusive fusion of coarse-grained knowledge to transmit and refine common knowledge among clients for personalization.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly propose the novel concept of a multi-granularity prompt.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments demonstrate the method's effectiveness in addressing spatial-temporal catastrophic forgetting and improving personalized performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: Personalized federated continual learning creates challenges in sharing and personalizing knowledge.
Prior methods overlook multi-granularity knowledge representation for spatial-temporal forgetting and personalization.
The method introduces coarse-grained global and fine-grained local prompts with distinct global-transfer and local-personalization roles.
Selective fusion aggregates distilled global-prompt knowledge through exclusive coarse-grained knowledge fusion.
Experiments report effectiveness for addressing spatial-temporal catastrophic forgetting and improving personalized performance.

source_observation.claim: Separating shared global knowledge from personalized local knowledge can address different spatial and temporal forgetting requirements.

interpretation.claim: Different knowledge granularities may need distinct transfer and personalization mechanisms.

application.claim: Federated continual learning systems could assign separate representations or update paths to common and client-specific knowledge.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this separation generalizes beyond the described setting.

source_observation.claim: Selective fusion of coarse-grained knowledge is reported to enhance personalization.

interpretation.claim: Restricting aggregation to selected shared knowledge may reduce interference between clients.

application.claim: Aggregation designs can selectively combine shared representations rather than merging all client knowledge uniformly.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the selection criteria or conditions under which selective fusion fails.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not provide implementation details for prompt construction or selective fusion.
The abstract does not report ablations, computational costs, or client and task conditions.
